items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: jazz instrumentation with people like Gary Burton and what’s his name, the bass player, Charlie Haden, Buell Neidlinger, that’s who I’m trying to think of.

ctx.x: In the pantheon of American music bluegrass is not all that old, is it? Or, the things I’ve read they stated 1940. Is that debatable?

Well Martin Heidegger had things to say about naming something and thereby changing its nature by assigning it a name. And so when there didn’t used to be bluegrass, which is what the situation that I heard in the 40s and 50s, it got along just fine. And all of a sudden one day somebody decided to give it a name. Well as soon as you give something a name you have to define it, and as soon as you define something you begin to exclude qualities that do not fit your definition and you begin to decide well does this…

But the 1-4-5, I’m sometimes surprised, if you look up blues on Wikipedia or in dictionaries, encyclopedias, to me the twelve-bar blues is the most elegant music form that I know of. And sometimes it gets short-shriffed in the definition of blues.
